One of the best experiences.
Jan 2026 • Family
Chef Didier & his team are hospitality at its finest. The warm interiors that greet guests from the moment you walk in have a charming character that made us feel excited for the culinary journey that’s to come. The ALC menu is extensive, and the venue also offers Tasting Menus for those who’d like to experience Chef Didier’s creations without too much thought. 

We went for the Signature Tasting menu. Although everything was absolutely delicious, I would say the appetiser platter was my favourite, offering around 6 to 7 dishes. I would recommend going for the signature tasting menu, and for the dessert trying out their three kinds of cake and ice cream, all home-made. The cinnamon ice cream was the star. 

We got a special chance to see the behind-the-scenes in the kitchen, as well as the top floor on a busy night. Their 2nd floor is a great escape in Hanoi for a private celebratory dinner.

The venue also offers the experience to see, and take home, spices made by Chef Didier himself. Their star anise and maki (a mix of salt, star anise and pepper) are great to use with home cooking.

We are glad we got the chance to have this meal, and feel first hand Chef Didier’s magic. We will be back!

uh...a Non-Return for us Viet Kieu Wanderers in their native land
Jan 2026 • Family
We went to Madame Hien based on the top reviews on Madame Hien. It was an utterly disappointing experience all around.
First Impression / Atmosphere. The decor is pleasant and unique enough, an alley way ambiance with the old world charm. 3.5 stars. After this first impression, we were seated at a corner table for 4. Both the table and 4 chairs were uncomfortable and unstable and wobbly due to the uneven surface of the alley way (which was paved with cobble stones)
Service. 2 star. The waiting staff did try hard to attend to the guests' needs, but they clearly lack the professional training of Front-of-House. After we ordered, there was a very long wait for us. It appeared that all of the other guests of other tables who arrived much after us were receiving the preferential (priority) of the FOH services. I must really wonder if it has anything to do with the fact that we were Viet Expats (Viet Kieu) visiting Ha Noi, as opposed to the Western Tourists (French especially, as the owner or chef is supposedly French). This is food for thought for chez Madame Hien. I mean Money is Money, and there should not be nationality or race attached to it as far as I am concerned.
Food. 1-star. One of the main dishes we ordered, Beef and Green Peppercorn was dredged in flour but not cooked properly, tasting quite doughy (as in raw flour), and is definitely not in any style of Vietnamese or French cooking. Generally, the food chez Madame Hien is - by any stretch of imagination - very far from representing the good fusion of Vietnamese and French cuisine.

In spite of all the great reviews (and what-not) for this restaurant, It is definitely not a return place for any of our future wandering back to Ha Noi.
